Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:10:1.hebrew: במכר לא קנה - כגון קרקע, דקי"ל לקמן (קידושין דף כו.) שהיא נקנה בכסף — אינו נקנה בכך, דלאו מידי יהיב ליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:10:1.english: In a sale, he does not acquire [it] - Such as land, which we establish later (Kiddushin 26a) is acquired with money — it is not acquired in this manner, as he did not give him anything.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:11:1.hebrew: יצא ידי נתינה - ומוכרה לכהנים, והדמים שלו. ולקמן פריך ממה נפשך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:11:1.english: He has fulfilled the obligation of giving - And he sells it to priests, and the money is his. And later on, [the Gemara] objects: Whichever way you look at it [how can this be]?

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:11:2.hebrew: ואסור לעשות כן - לפי שבשכר זה יתן לו שאר תרומותיו, והוי האי כהן כקונה תרומה בשכרו, ומסייע בבית הגרנות שיתנו לו התרומה. ותנן בבכורות (דף כו:): כהנים המסייעים בבית הגרנות אין נותנין להם תרומה ומעשרות בשכרן, ואם עשו כן — חללו, ועליהם הכתוב אומר (מלאכי ב׳:ח׳): שחתם ברית הלוי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:11:2.english: But it is prohibited to do this - Because as payment for this, [the owner] will give him the rest of his terumot, and this priest is like one who purchases teruma with his wage, and [like a priest who] assists at the threshing floor so that they will give him the teruma. And we learned [in a mishna] in Bekhorot (26b): Priests who assist at the threshing floor — one may not give them teruma and tithes as their wage; and if they did so, they have profaned [them], and concerning them the verse states (Malachi 2:8): "You have corrupted the covenant of Levi."

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:13:1.english: [If] he did not return it, he has not fulfilled [his obligation] - For it is [considered] stolen property retroactively.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:14:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רב אשי - ודאי בכולהו אמר רבא דקונה, לבר מאשה כו'. והאי לחליפין דמי — כקנין בסודר, דאינו אלא אוחז בה ומחזירו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:14:1.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said - Certainly, in all of them Rava said that [one] acquires, except for a woman, etc. And this is similar to symbolic exchange — like an acquisition with a kerchief, where [the recipient] merely grasps it and returns it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:1:1.hebrew: לא אמר כלום - להתגרשה, אם כתב לשון זה בגט, שאין זה לשון גירושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:1:1.english: He has said nothing - [meaning] for her to be divorced, if he wrote this wording in the bill of divorce, for this is not an expression of divorce.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:1:2.hebrew: הרי את מותרת - לשון גירושין הוא, ולא לשון שחרור דשפחה; דאי בת חורין משוה לה, אינה מותרת לעבדים. אבל לשון גט הוא לאשה, שמתירה לכל שהיתה אסורה לו על ידו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:1:2.english: You are hereby permitted - This is an expression of divorce, and not an expression of emancipation for a maidservant; for if he makes her a free woman, she is not permitted to slaves. Rather, it is an expression of a bill of divorce for a woman, as it permits her to everyone to whom she had been forbidden on his account.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:2:2.english: With regard to work - That the work of her hands should be hers.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:4:2.hebrew: לגמרי - אפי' לשחרור גופו, ומותר בבת חורין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:4:2.english: Entirely - Even for the emancipation of his person, and he is permitted [to marry] a free woman.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:5:1.hebrew: יצא לחירות - ואע"ג דקי"ל (גיטין דף מד.) קונסין אותו לפדותו מן העובד כוכבים עד עשרה בדמיו, דאפקעיה ממצות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:5:1.english: He is emancipated - And even though we maintain (Gittin 44a) that we penalize him to redeem him from the gentile for up to ten times his value because he removed him from the mitzvot, [the slave nevertheless goes free].

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:5:2.hebrew: וצריך גט שחרור - להתירו בבת חורין, משום דעובד כוכבים גופו לא קני, דכתיב: "מהם תקנו" — אתם קונין מהם, ולא הם קונים מכם, ולא הם קונים זה את זה (שם דף לח.):
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:5:2.english: And requires a bill of manumission - To permit him [to marry] a free woman, because a gentile does not acquire [ownership of] his body, as it is written: "From them shall you buy" [Leviticus 25:44] — you acquire from them, but they do not acquire from you, nor do they acquire from one another (ibid., 38a).

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:6:1.hebrew: בד"א - שצריך גט שחרור, שלא כתב עליו אונו כשמכרו לעובד כוכבים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:6:1.english: In what case is this said - [That] he requires a bill of manumission [applies in a case] where he did not write his document [ono] for him when he sold him to a gentile.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:6:2.english: His document [ono] - An expression for a document.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:6:3.english: When you escape from him - From the gentile.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:6:4.english: I have no business with you - Evidently, it is an expression of emancipation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:7:1.english: One who betroths with a loan - Where he said, "Be betrothed to me with the loan that I lent you."

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:7:2.hebrew: אינה מקודשת - דקיחה משדה עפרון גמרינן, דיהיב מידי בשעת קידושין. ומלוה להוצאה ניתנה, וכבר הן שלה, ומעות אחרים היא חייבת לו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:7:2.english: She is not betrothed - For we derive [the law of] 'taking' from the field of Ephron, that he gives something at the time of betrothal. And a loan is given to be spent, and [the money] is already hers, and she owes him other money.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:7:3.english: With the benefit of a loan - [The Gemara] goes on to explain it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:8:1.hebrew: אילימא דאזקפה - מעיקרא ארבעה בחמשה, והשתא אמר לה: "התקדשי לי בזוז חמישי":
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:8:1.english: If we say that he established it - Initially, four [zuz] for five, and now he said to her: "Be betrothed to me with the fifth zuz."

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:8:2.english: This is full-fledged interest - And why did [Abaye] call it an evasion of interest?

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:8:3.english: This is the reading: "And furthermore, this is a loan" - For even this zuz, she is already obligated [to pay].

Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:9:1.hebrew: לא צריכא דארווח לה זמן - הלואתו, ואמר לה: התקדשי בהנאה זו שאת היית נותנת פרוטה לאדם שיפייסני על כך, או לי, ואפי' לאגר נטר לא דמי כלל. ואם פירש לה כך — מקודשת. והערמת רבית הוא דהויא, ולא רבית גמור, דלא קץ לה מידי ולא מידי שקל מינה. וכ"ש אם מחל לה כל המלוה, ואמר לה: התקדשי לי בהנאת מחילה זו — דהשתא הוא דקא יהיב לה הך פרוטה דהנאת מלוה; אבל כי מקדש לה בעיקר המעות — לאו מידי יהיב לה, שכבר הם ברשותה והם שלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6b:9:1.english: No, [it is] necessary [in a case] where he extended the time for her - [Of] his loan. And he said to her: "Be betrothed [to me] with this benefit, that you would have given a perutah to a person to placate me concerning this, or to me." And it is not even similar to payment for waiting at all. And if he specified [this] to her, she is betrothed. And it is [only] circumvention of interest, and not full-fledged interest, for he did not fix anything upon her, nor did he take anything from her. And all the more so if he forgave her the entire loan and said to her: "Be betrothed to me with the benefit of this forgiveness," for it is now that he is giving her this perutah of benefit from the loan; but when he betroths her with the principal of the money, he is not giving her anything, as they are already in her possession and are hers.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 6b:13:1.hebrew: לא החזירו לא יצא - וא"ת: אמאי לא יצא, הא לא הוה תנאי כפול? וי"ל: דאיכא תנאי דלא בעי כפול, כגון הכא, שהיה דעתו שיברך חבירו על אתרוג שלו. וגדולה מזאת אמרו (לקמן קידושין דף מט: ושם) בההוא גברא דזבין נכסיה אדעתא למיסק לארעא דישראל, ולא פירש ולא מידי, וסוף לא סליק, בעי למיהדר, ואמר רב הונא: הוי דברים שבלב, ואינם דברים; א"כ משמע: דוקא משום דלא פירש, אבל אם פירש — הוי תנאי, אע"ג דלא כפליה. וה"נ איתא במי שמת (ב"ב דף קמז.) גבי ש"מ שאמר: "כמדומה אני שאשתי מעוברת, אבל עכשיו שאינה מעוברת — נכסי לפלוני", לסוף נתגלה שהיתה מעוברת, וקאמר התם דלא הוי מתנה, משום דמעיקרא לא היה בדעתו ליתנם לאותו פלוני אם היתה אשתו מעוברת; ה"נ לא בעינן תנאי כפול, כיון שהיה בדעתו לכך. וא"ת: ובלא החזירו, אמאי לא יצא? והא הוי תנאי ומעשה בדבר אחד, והתנאי בטל, כדאמרי' התם (גיטין דף עה.): מכדי כל תנאי מהיכא ילפינן? מתנאי בני גד ובני ראובן, והתם תנאי בדבר אחד ומעשה בדבר אחר הוה! וי"ל: התם לא הוי מסקנא הכי, ואיכא שינויי אחריני. א"נ י"ל: הא דלא מהני תנאי ומעשה בדבר אחד, היינו כששניהם סותרים זה את זה, כי ההיא ד"על מנת שתחזירי לי את הנייר" דפרק מי שאחזו (שם), דהתם ס"ד דכל האומר ע"מ לאו כאומר מעכשיו דמי, ונמצא שאינה מגורשת עד שמחזרת הנייר, ואז אינו שלה; אבל הכא סבר דכל האומר על מנת — כאומר מעכשיו דמי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 6b:13:1.english: "[If] he did not return it, he has not fulfilled [his obligation]" - And if you say: Why has he not fulfilled [his obligation]? After all, there was no doubled stipulation [tenai kaful]! And one can answer: There are stipulations that do not require doubling, such as here, where his intention was [only] that his fellow recite the blessing over his etrog. And greater than this they said (below, Kiddushin 49b, and there [Ketubot 97a]): in the case of a certain man who sold his property with the intention of ascending to the Land of Israel, and he did not state anything [explicitly], and in the end he did not ascend [and] wanted to retract [the sale], and Rav Huna said: [These] are matters in the heart, and matters in the heart are not words [i.e., have no legal standing]; if so, this implies that [this is] specifically because he did not state [it explicitly], but had he stated [it], it would be a [valid] stipulation even though he did not double it. And so too it is found in [the chapter] Mi SheMet (Bava Batra 147a) regarding a dying man [shekhiv mera] who said: "I thought that my wife was pregnant, but now that she is not pregnant, my property [is given] to so-and-so," [and] in the end it was discovered that she was pregnant, and [the Gemara] says there that it is not a [valid] gift, because from the outset it was not his intention to give them to that so-and-so if his wife were pregnant; so too here, we do not require a doubled stipulation, since his intention was for this [purpose]. And if you say: And when he did not return it, why has he not fulfilled [his obligation]? For isn't this [a case of] a stipulation and an act concerning the same thing [tenai uma'aseh bedavar echad], and [in such a case] the stipulation is void? As we say there (Gittin 75a): "After all, from where do we derive [the rules of] all stipulations? From the stipulation of the children of Gad and the children of Reuven; and there, the stipulation was concerning one thing and the act was concerning another thing!" And one can answer: There, that is not the conclusion [of the Gemara], and there are other resolutions. Alternatively, one can answer: That which a stipulation and an act concerning the same thing are not effective applies [only] when the two contradict one another, like that [case] of "on the condition that you return the paper to me" in the chapter Mi SheAchazo (ibid.). For there, the Gemara initially thought that whoever says "on the condition that" is not like one who says "from now," and it turns out that she is not divorced until she returns the paper, and then it is not hers; but here, [Rava] maintains that whoever says "on the condition that" is like one who says "from now."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 6b:13:2.hebrew: ואם לאו לא יצא - והא דאמר במסכת סוכה (דף מא:): אתרוג היה לו לר"ג, נטלו ר' יהושע ויצא בו, ונתנו לר"ע, ויצא בו ר"ע, והחזיר לר"ג, ודייקי' מינה: מתנה על מנת להחזיר שמה מתנה — אע"פ שר' יהושע לא החזירו לר"ג, דעתו של ר"ג היה לכך, שלא היה חושש אלא שיחזור לידו אחר שיצאו כולם:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 6b:13:2.english: "And if not, he has not fulfilled [his obligation]" - And as for that which [the Gemara] says in tractate Sukkah (41b): Rabban Gamliel had an etrog; Rabbi Yehoshua took it and fulfilled [his obligation] with it, and gave it to Rabbi Akiva, and Rabbi Akiva fulfilled [his obligation] with it and returned it to Rabban Gamliel, and we infer from it that a gift [given] on the condition that it is returned is called a gift — [this is because] even though Rabbi Yehoshua did not return it to Rabban Gamliel, Rabban Gamliel's intention was for this, as he was concerned only that it return to his hand after all of them had fulfilled [their obligation].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 6b:14:1.hebrew: לבר מאשה לפי שאין אשה נקנית בחליפין - וא"ת: במאי דמו לחליפין? אי משום דחליפין הדרי — הא בחליפין גופייהו אמר בנדרים פרק השותפין (נדרים דף מח:) דאי תפיס לה מיתפסי! ונראה לר"י: דלאו חליפין הוא, ומדרבנן הוא דלא הוו קידושין — לפי שדרך העולם להחזיר חליפין, והני כעין חליפין דמי, ואתי למימר: "אשה נקנית בחליפין"; הילכך אפקעינהו רבנן לקידושין מינה. תדע: דאי כחליפין דמו, במכר היאך קנה בהאי מנה? הא אין מטבע נעשה חליפין! וכן בפדיון הבן, למה יהא בנו פדוי בחליפין? הלא "כסף ה' שקלים" כתיב, ולא חליפין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 6b:14:1.english: "Except for a woman, because a woman cannot be acquired through chalipin [symbolic exchange]" - And if you say: In what way is [a gift on condition of return] similar to chalipin? If [you suggest that it is] because [the object used for] chalipin is returned — but regarding chalipin itself, [the Gemara] says in Nedarim, chapter HaShutafin (48b), that if he seized it, it is seized! And it appears to the Ri that it is not [actual] chalipin, and it is [only] by rabbinic law that it is not a [valid] betrothal — because it is the way of the world to return [the object used for] chalipin, and this resembles chalipin, and [people] might come to say: "A woman can be acquired through chalipin"; therefore, the Sages abrogated the betrothal from her. Know [that this is so], for if it were [legally] like chalipin, in a sale how could [the buyer] acquire [property] with this maneh? Surely a coin cannot be made [an instrument of] chalipin! And so too with the redemption of the firstborn, why should his son be redeemed through chalipin? Is it not written: "The money of five shekels" [Numbers 3:47], and not chalipin?

Tosafot on Kiddushin 6b:3:1.hebrew: אשה דלא קני ליה גופה לכ"ש - אע"ג דגבי הרי את בת חורין לא מהני מק"ו, היינו משום דלא שייך חירות באשה, ולא עביד ק"ו אלא מלשונות דשייכי הכא והכא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 6b:3:1.english: "A woman, whose body he does not own, all the more so" - Even though regarding "You are hereby a free woman," it is not effective by an a fortiori argument, that is because [the concept of] freedom does not apply to a woman; and an a fortiori argument is made only from expressions that apply both here and there.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 6b:6:1.hebrew: כשתברח ממנו - כלומר, מן העובד כוכבים. אבל אינו רוצה לומר: "כשתברח ממני, מעכשיו אין לי עסק בך" — א"כ, יהיה מיד בן חורין ויתחייב במצות, ולא יוכל לקיימו בבית העובד כוכבים; נמצא שרע לו מה שכותב עליו אונו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 6b:6:1.english: "When you escape from him" - That is to say, from the gentile. But he does not mean to say: "When you escape from me, from now on I have no business with you" — for if so, he would immediately be a free man and obligated in the mitzvot, and he would not be able to observe them in the house of the gentile; it would thus turn out that what [the master] writes for him in his document [ono] is detrimental to him.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 6b:9:1.hebrew: דארווח לה זימנא - פי' בקונטרס: שהיתה חייבת לו, ונתן לה זמן, ואמר לה: "התקדשי לי בהנאה זו שאת היית נותנת לאדם פרוטה שיפייסני על כך". ואם פירש לה כך — מקודשת. והערמת רבית הוא דהויא, ולא רבית גמור, דלא קץ לה ולא מידי שקיל מינה. וכ"ש אם מחל לה כל המלוה, ואמר לה: "התקדשי לי בהנאת מחילה זו" — מקודשת; אבל כי מקדשה בעיקר המעות — לאו מידי יהיב לה, שכבר הם שלה וברשותה. ומה שפי' דרבית קצוצה לא הוי כיון שאין האשה נותנת לאיש כלום — לא נהירא: כיון שהוא נותן לה זה פרוטה בקידושין ולא נתן לה כלום, הוי כאילו נתנה לו פרוטה ממש, והוי רבית גמור! וכי ההיא (ב"מ דף סב:) ד"מנה אין לי, חטין במנה יש לי" שייך לקרות הערמת רבית, שמערים דלא הוי אגר נטר ליה. לכן פר"ת דאיירי הכא: שהיתה חייבת מעות לאדם אחר, והגיע זמנו לפרוע, ובא זה ונותן למלוה פרוטה לארווחי לה זימנא, וקידשה באותה הנאה. ואם תאמר: אמאי אסור לעשות כן מפני הערמת רבית? והא אמר בפרק איזהו נשך (בבא מציעא דף סט:): "שרי ליה לאיניש למימר לחבריה: שקול ד' זוזי ואוזפי לפלוני זוזי, דלא אסרה תורה אלא רבית הבאה מלוה למלוה"? וי"ל: היינו שאין הלוה נותן כלום לנותן, אבל אם היה נותן — היה נראה כשלוחו, ואסור; דכי נמי אמרינן התם באיזהו נשך (שם): "שרי ליה לאיניש למימר לחבריה: שקול ד' זוזי ואמור לפלוני דלוזפן זוזי" — היינו כשאין המקבל נותן כלום למלוה, כי אם היה נותן — היה נראה כשלוחו, ואסור. וא"ת: אמאי מוקי לה בארווח לה? בתחילת הלוואה היה יכול להעמיד, דבהנאת מלוה מקודשת — כגון שהמקדש נותן למלוה פרוטה להלוות לה מעות, ובאותה פרוטה נתקדשה לו! וי"ל: "בהנאת מלוה" משמע מלוה שהיתה עליו כבר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 6b:9:1.english: Where he extended the time for her - Rashi explains: That she was indebted to him, and he gave her [more] time [to repay], and said to her: "Be betrothed to me through this benefit, for which you would have given a perutah to someone so that he would appease me regarding this." And if he explained this to her, she is betrothed. And this is [only] an artifice of interest, and not full-fledged interest, since he did not fix [an interest payment] for her, nor did he take anything from her. And all the more so, if he forgave her the entire loan and said to her: "Be betrothed to me through the benefit of this forgiveness," she is betrothed; but when he betroths her with the principal of the money, he gives her nothing, for it is already hers and in her possession. And that which [Rashi] explained, that it is not fixed interest because the woman gives the man nothing, is difficult [to accept]: since he gives her this [benefit worth a] perutah for betrothal and did not give her anything [else], it is as though she gave him an actual perutah, and it is full-fledged interest! And [it is only] in a case like that one (Bava Metzia 62b) of "I do not have a maneh, [but] I have wheat worth a maneh," that it is appropriate to call it an artifice of interest, where one employs an artifice so that it does not appear as a fee for waiting. Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explained that we are dealing here with [a case where] she owed money to another person, and the time [for her] to repay arrived, and this [man] came and gave the lender a perutah to extend the time for her, and betrothed her with that benefit. And if you say: Why is it prohibited to do so on account of an artifice of interest? But didn't [the Gemara] say in the chapter [entitled] Eizehu Neshekh (Bava Metzia 69b): "It is permitted for a person to say to his fellow: Take four dinars and lend money to so-and-so, for the Torah prohibited only interest that comes from the borrower to the lender"? And one can say: That is [only] where the borrower gives nothing to the giver; but if he were to give [something to the giver], [the giver] would appear as his agent, and it would be prohibited. For similarly, when we say there in Eizehu Neshekh (ibid.): "It is permitted for a person to say to his fellow: Take four dinars and tell so-and-so to lend us money," that is [only] when the recipient gives nothing to the lender; for if he were to give [anything to the lender], he would appear as his agent, and it would be prohibited. And if you say: Why does [the Gemara] establish [the case of "benefit of a loan"] where he extended the time for her? It could have established that she is betrothed through the benefit of a loan at the beginning of a loan, such as where the betrother gives the lender a perutah to lend her money, and she was betrothed to him with that perutah! And one can say: "Through the benefit of a loan" implies a loan that was already upon him [i.e., upon the borrower].
